content.rationale: a conformance check over the page interface, realized as a runnable test because every clause is an observable of the artifact: the check reads the interface through its own exported names (the region selectors, the two identity attributes, the emphasis vocabulary and the presentation) and asserts clause by clause what the recorded prerequisites promise. Against vylxkuxr, that the graph is presented inside a page: the interface names a region per page area, each reached by a selector of its own, and every area its own views attach to is one it names. Against krvyoumy, that malformed documents are contained: the check drives an implementer of the interface (the presentation state that attaches to a StatesView, whose module the page provides) instead of a presentation it builds itself, hands it the problems a read reports as loaded's warnings argument, and asserts that state() hands back exactly those problems, unchanged and one per omitted document, so a file name and its problem reach the banner region, that an omitted document is not reported as a failed read, and that the node already drawn stays on the canvas so the remaining nodes still render. It does not read LoadedNodeGraph's warnings: it compares the presentation with the problems it passed to the implementer's own loaded entry point, the entry point by which a read hands its problems to the presentation. Against qmsmvrnr, that the interface is defined over the graph model, its order and its geometry without pinning a value that model's interface does not fix. The clauses face the two requirement-sentence prerequisites as conformance and the code prerequisite as a test, and one runnable check covers all three edges; it reads nothing from the page, the stylesheets or the documents on disk, which are the subjects of other checks, so it stays a check of how the interface carries its contract rather than of what it renders One more clause family joins them for the edge this round adds. wzsxvmvw states, in requirement sentences, when the viewer centres and where the viewport lands: a trigger on focus moving onto a node and a trigger on the activation of a listed relationship id, the axis terms that decide where a centring move stops, and the moves the rule leaves alone. The subject is the contract artifact, so the two endpoints place this edge in the structured-to-code cell and its check is conformance over the artifact, carried as a runnable clause in a contract check of its own beside this one. Of that rule the interface carries one part and no more: that the page has a declared way to ask the interaction to bring a selected node into view. The rule's triggers, its axis terms and its limits are performed by the interaction state, whose behaviour is another decision's artifact; a clause that drove a centring would fail on what the interface was never meant to contain, so this clause checks the declaration - that the interface declares the request - and nothing about the move, and the declaration alone satisfies it, before any centring exists. The clause is structural because a declaration is what the interface's part of the rule is: the check reads the contract module as a declaration, its exported interfaces with the members each of them declares and the declared parameters and parameter types, and asks one question of it. It locates the interface the page holds for the interaction by two members that interface already declares, the node selection (ltrnmrsr) and the viewport the interaction moves, then takes the requests that interface declares over one node identity and requires exactly one of them beyond the requests already recorded there, select (ltrnmrsr) and focusNode (ruqsmuxz): one, because the page asks the interaction to bring a node into view one way, and a second such request is a second way the page names a node to centre on, which this edge does not settle, while none leaves the page with no way to ask at all. The request it finds must also be one the page must make: the interface does not declare the member optional, the member's declared type does not admit undefined or null as the whole member, and the node identity it takes cannot be left out. A request the page may leave out, or make without naming a node, does not name the node a centring move centres on, and that is the rule's own subject - the node its trigger identifies, already chosen when the move starts - so a declaration that can be made without naming one is not the interface's part of it. A nullish arm inside the parameter's own type stays permitted, since select and focusNode already take the cleared case and a parameter that must be passed and may be null still has the page name something; what is refused is the absence of the request, not the cleared case in its argument. The clause keeps, too, the members the recorded prerequisites already declare on that interface - the selection and its clearing (select, selected, clearSelection), the keyboard focus and its traversal (focusNode, focused, focusStep), the viewport and the moves on it (viewport, panBy, zoomAt, zoomAboutCentre, fitGraph), a node's move (moveNodeBy), the graph swap (setGraph) and the teardown (dispose) - and requires that they be declared still. They are recorded facts, so naming them settles nothing this edge does not already take as given, and they are what the request is made beside: an interface gutted of the members the move is performed with, and given the request in their place, has replaced what the interface was rather than added what this edge adds. The list is the interface's own members as the artifact already declares them, not a shape imposed on it, so a declaration that puts the request beside every recorded member is untouched by the clause. Both facts the clause now fixes are properties of the declaration's shape and not of the member's name, which is what a check that names nothing can honestly pin: whether a member is declared, how many such members the interface declares, and whether the page must call it are read from the declaration alone, without deciding what the member is called, what its parameter is called or what it returns. The rule says the viewer centres on the node its trigger identifies; one request that names a node whenever the page makes it is that, read off the declaration, and neither cardinality nor non-optionality fixes a choice the artifact was free to make. Nothing more is claimed: a request that takes the node identity and means something else still passes, and that is the accepted price of naming nothing. A request added as an exported free function beside the interface is not counted, because the scan reads the interface bodies alone and the page can ask the interaction only for what the interface it composes declares; a request declared by an interface the located one extends is counted, because the page holding that interface can call it all the same. The added member is named nowhere, neither in the clause nor here: its name and its exact shape are the artifact's to settle, and a gate that fixed a name would be deciding the decision's content and would fail the independence test the first time the drafter chose otherwise, reading the dependent back to itself instead of checking what it adds. What the clause does fix is the node identity the request must take - an id of the model the interface is defined over (qmsmvrnr), a string and nothing a node id cannot be, the same identity select already accepts, with the cleared case the selection admits permitted since a request naming a node neither needs nor excludes it in its type; the member's name, its parameter's name and its return type are left open and appear only in the check's output, as does the interface the request is declared on. The check's satisfying path is stated so that it holds whether or not the artifact declares the request: over a declaration of its own, and over the artifact as a relative property - one request inserted under a name the source does not already carry adds exactly one to the count the clause reads - so the clause cannot be red because of the check's own fixture and no candidate is failed for declaring what the clause asks for. The check reads nothing from the page composition, the stylesheets or a render, so it stays a check of how the interface carries the request rather than of what the move does, and the behaviour of the move stays a check of another edge.
